sentences.text: 1. Petitioner has filed this writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India making a prayer to appoint retired Judicial Arbitrator to settle the dispute between petitioner and respondents.
Further prayer was made to quash order dated 20.12.2023 contained in Annexure P/2 passed by respondent no.3 i.e. Deputy Chief Engineer (Nirman), Western Railway, Indore.

entities.text: Deputy Chief Engineer (Nirman), Western Railway, Indore
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts of the case are that petitioner was owner of the land bearing Khasra No. 601/01 area 0.380 hectare, Khasra No. 599 area 0.060 hectare, Khasra No. 600/2/2 area 0.100 hectare, Khasra No. 600/2/1 area 0.060 hectare, Khasra No. 600/1/1 Area 0.640 hectare and Khasra No. 598 Area 0.240 hectare situated in village Mortkka District Khandwa.

Said land is acquired under the provisions of Railway Amendment Act, 2008 (for short "Act of 2008") for special railway NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:45305 2 WP-19156-2024 project for gauge conversion of Ratlam - Indore-Dr. Ambedkar Nagar- Khandwa Aman Project.
It is submitted that remedy under the Act of 2008 could not be availed as there was no vide scale publication and notification in news paper.
SDM revenue has passed proposed award on 20.12.2023 without giving any opportunity to petitioner and other land owners.
It is submitted that if party has aggrieved by an award then such party will have remedy under Section 20A(6) of the Act of 2008 for appointment of Arbitrator.
Provisions of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 will apply as laid down in Section 20A (7) of the Act of 2008.
There was procedural defect in acquiring the land in question and despite request Arbitrator has not been appointed.

Rights of natural justice have been violated and, therefore,
impugned order be quashed.

sentences.text: 3. Heard learned counsel appearing for the petitioner.
4. Railway Amendment Act came into force on 31.1.2008.

As per said Act, Special Railway project means project notified by Central Government for providing national infrastructure for public purpose and specified time frame to cover one or more States or Union Territories.
Notification for acquisition of land is to be issued under Section 20(A) (1) of the Act of 2008.
Substance of notification is to be published in news paper as per Section 20(A) (4) of the Act of 2008.

As per Section 20(D)(1) of the Act of 2008, any person interested in the land may file his objection within a period of 30 days from the date of publication of the notification under sub section (1) of Section 20A of the Act of 2008.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:45305 3 WP-19156-2024

Objection shall be filed before competent authority in writing and shall be decided by competent authority thereafter report shall be submitted to Central Government by notification that land is to be acquired for public purpose.
After publication of declaration under Section 20(E)(1) of the Act of 2008 land shall vest absolutely in Central Government free from all encumbrances.
Where land is acquired under the provisions of Amendment Act of 2008, interested person shall be paid compensation as determined by competent authority under Section 20(F)(1) of the Act of 2008.
Award is to be passed within a period of one year from the date of publication of declaration.

If amount determined by competent authority under sub section (1) of 20 (F) of the Act of 2008 is not acceptable to either of the party on application or by either of the party amount be determined by Arbitrator to be appointed by Central Government as per Section 20(F)(6) of the Act of 2008.
Section 20(F)(7) of the Act of 2008 further lays down that provision of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 shall apply to every arbitration under the Act.
As per Section 20(F)(6) of the Act of 2008, if a land owner is not satisfied with compensation awarded by competent authority then he may file application for appointment of arbitrator.
Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is made applicable to the procedure passed under the Act of 2008.

5. Since statutory arbitration is provided under the Act and if Central Government fails to appoint Arbitrator, the petitioner is having NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:45305 4 WP-19156-2024 remedy to file an application for appointment of Arbitrator under Section 11(6) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
Writ Petition is not maintainable.
6. Petition is dismissed.

(VISHAL DHAGAT) JUDGE AD/
